53506-a-collection-of-kacha-ri-folk-tale.description: A book by J. D. Anderson,. uriously like the Assamese syntax. As an instance of this I have taken down (see page 1) an accused person's statement in both Assamese and Kachári. The Kachári version is, literally, a word-for-word translation of the Assamese. I can think of no other two languages in which it would be possible to translate a long statement word for word out of one into the other and yet be idiomatic.

arxiv-2103-00755.title: Adaptive Sampling for Minimax Fair Classification
arxiv-2103-00755.creator: Shubhanshu Shekhar, Greg Fields, Mohammad Ghavamzadeh, Tara Javidi
arxiv-2103-00755.description: Abstract Machine learning models trained on uncurated datasets can often end up adversely affecting inputs belonging to underrepresented groups. To address this issue, we consider the problem of adaptively constructing training sets which allow us to learn classifiers that are fair in a minimax sense.

arxiv-2109-04582.title: Scattering searches for dark matter in subhalos: neutron stars, cosmic rays, and old rocks
arxiv-2109-04582.creator: Joseph Bramante, Bradley J. Kavanagh, Nirmal Raj
arxiv-2109-04582.description: Abstract In many cosmologies dark matter clusters on sub-kiloparsec scales and forms compact subhalos, in which the majority of Galactic dark matter could reside. Null results in direct detection experiments since their advent four decades ago could then be the result of extremely rare encounters between the Earth and these subhalos.

arxiv-2202-05549.title: Lightning: Scaling the GPU Programming Model Beyond a Single GPU
arxiv-2202-05549.creator: Stijn Heldens, Pieter Hijma, Ben van Werkhoven, Jason Maassen, Rob V. van Nieuwpoort
arxiv-2202-05549.description: Abstract The GPU programming model is primarily aimed at the development of applications that run one GPU. However, this limits the scalability of GPU code to the capabilities of a single GPU in terms of compute power and memory capacity.

arxiv-2208-08218.title: ODformer: Spatial-Temporal Transformers for Long Sequence Origin-Destination Matrix Forecasting Against Cross Application Scenario
arxiv-2208-08218.creator: Jin Huang, Bosong Huang, Weihao Yu, Jing Xiao, Ruzhong Xie, Ke Ruan
arxiv-2208-08218.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jin Huang, Bosong Huang, Weihao Yu, Jing Xiao, Ruzhong Xie, Ke Ruan. Origin-Destination (OD) matrices record directional flow data between pairs of OD regions. The intricate spatiotemporal dependency in the matrices makes the OD matrix forecasting (ODMF) problem not only intractable but also non-trivial. However, most of the related methods are designed for very short sequence time series forecasting in specific application scenarios, which cannot meet the requirements of the variation in scenarios and forecasting length of practical applications.

arxiv-2212-00736.title: An exponentially-growing family of universal quantum circuits
arxiv-2212-00736.creator: Mo Kordzanganeh, Pavel Sekatski, Leonid Fedichkin, Alexey Melnikov
arxiv-2212-00736.description: Abstract Quantum machine learning has become an area of growing interest but has certain theoretical and hardware-specific limitations. Notably, the problem of vanishing gradients, or barren plateaus, renders the training impossible for circuits with high qubit counts, imposing a limit on the number of qubits that data scientists can use for solving problems.

arxiv-2401-17925.title: Interoperable Workflows by Exchanging Grid-Based Data between Quantum-Chemical Program Packages
arxiv-2401-17925.description: Abstract Quantum-chemical subsystem and embedding methods require complex workflows that may involve multiple quantum-chemical program packages. Moreover, such workflows require the exchange of voluminous data that goes beyond simple quantities such as molecular structures and energies. Here, we describe our approach for addressing this interoperability challenge by exchanging electron densities and embedding potentials as grid-based data.

arxiv-2403-15716.title: Distributed Robust Learning based Formation Control of Mobile Robots based on Bioinspired Neural Dynamics Thanks: This paper is accepted by IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Vehicles , DOI: 10.1109/TIV.2024.3380000 This work was supported by the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council (NSER
arxiv-2403-15716.creator: Zhe Xu, Tao Yan
arxiv-2403-15716.description: Abstract This paper addresses the challenges of distributed formation control in multiple mobile robots, introducing a novel approach that enhances real-world practicability. We first introduce a distributed estimator using a variable structure and cascaded design technique, eliminating the need for derivative information to improve the real time performance.

arxiv-2409-11804.title: Conformal Prediction for Manifold-based Source Localization with Gaussian Processes
arxiv-2409-11804.creator: Vadim Rozenfeld and Bracha Laufer Goldshtein
arxiv-2409-11804.description: Abstract We address the problem of UQ ( UQ ) in the localization of a sound source within adverse acoustic environments. Estimating the position of the source is influenced by various factors, such as noise and reverberation, leading to significant uncertainty.

arxiv-2411-06498.title: Barriers to Complexity-Theoretic Proofs that Achieving AGI Using Machine Learning is Intractable
arxiv-2411-06498.creator: Michael Guerzhoy
arxiv-2411-06498.description: Abstract A recent paper [ VRGA+24 ] claims to have proved that achieving human-like intelligence using learning from data is intractable in a complexity-theoretic sense. We point out that the proof relies on an unjustified assumption about the distribution of (input, output) pairs in the data.

arxiv-2504-18164.title: Recent advances in data-driven methods for degradation modelling across applications
arxiv-2504-18164.creator: Anna Jarosz-Kozyro, Jerzy Baranowski
arxiv-2504-18164.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Anna Jarosz-Kozyro, Jerzy Baranowski. Understanding degradation is crucial for ensuring the longevity and performance of materials, systems, and organisms. To illustrate the similarities across applications, this article provides a review of data-based method in materials science, engineering, and medicine. The methods analyzed in this paper include regression analysis, factor analysis, cluster analysis, Markov Chain Monte Carlo, Bayesian statistics, hidden Markov models, nonparametric Bayesian modeling of time series, supervised learning, and deep learning.

arxiv-2505-05659.title: V-EfficientNets: Vector-Valued Efficiently Scaled Convolutional Neural Network Models Thanks: Guilherme Vieira acknowledges the post-doctorate scholarship granted by Universidade Estadual de Campinas (UNICAMP). Marcos Eduardo Valle acknowledges financial support from the National Council for Scienti
arxiv-2505-05659.creator: 1 st Guilherme Vieira Neto, 2 nd Marcos Eduardo Valle
arxiv-2505-05659.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by 1 st Guilherme Vieira Neto, 2 nd Marcos Eduardo Valle. EfficientNet models are convolutional neural networks optimized for parameter allocation by jointly balancing network width, depth, and resolution. Renowned for their exceptional accuracy, these models have become a standard for image classification tasks across diverse computer vision benchmarks. While traditional neural networks learn correlations between feature channels during training, vector-valued neural networks inherently treat multidimensional data as coherent entities, taking for granted the inter-channel relationships.

arxiv-2509-13555.title: A Computational Picture of Hydride Formation and Dissipation In Nb SRF Cavities
arxiv-2509-13555.creator: Aiden V. Harbick, Mark K. Transtrum, Nathan S. Sitaraman, Tomas A. Arias, Matthias U. Liepe
arxiv-2509-13555.description: Abstract Research linking surface hydrides to Q-disease, and the subsequent development of methods to eliminate surface hydrides, is one of the great successes of SRF cavity R&D. We use time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau to extend the theory of hydride dissipation to sub-surface hydrides. Just as surface hydrides cause Q-disease behavior, we show that sub-surface hydrides cause high-field Q-slope (HFQS) behavior.

arxiv-2602-15355.title: DAV-GSWT: Diffusion-Active-View Sampling for Data-Efficient Gaussian Splatting Wang Tiles
arxiv-2602-15355.creator: Rong Fu, Jiekai Wu, Haiyun Wei, Yee Tan Jia, Wenxin Zhang, Yang Li, Xiaowen Ma, Wangyu Wu, Simon Fong
arxiv-2602-15355.description: Abstract The emergence of 3D Gaussian Splatting has fundamentally redefined the capabilities of photorealistic neural rendering by enabling high-throughput synthesis of complex environments. While procedural methods like Wang Tiles have recently been integrated to facilitate the generation of expansive landscapes, these systems typically remain constrained by a reliance on densely sampled exemplar reconstructions.
